text:
alex: Heads-up — running a micro-check on trace schema compactness, found really high cardinality fields (ev.metadata.service_version) blowing up our indexing. Anyone else seen this?

maria: Yep, saw it in prod yesterday during a debug session. Range query latencies spiked.

jon: Is this the pre-enrich vs post-enrich tradeoff again? We currently keep the full SDK payload in trace.envelope which is convenient but heavy.

ravi: Short recap: 2 main options we keep juggling: 1) full rich envelope (everything searchable inline) vs 2) minimal canonical spans + separate enrichment doc. Tradeoffs are query latency, storage, and join complexity.

taylor: For cost attribution specifically, duplication of billing_key across every span is expensive. We should decide whether billing should live only on root.

alex: Example of the problematic shape:
```json
{
  "trace_id":"...",
  "spans":[{"id":"s1","service":"api","attrs":{...}}, ...],
  "ev.metadata":{"service_version":"2025-11.1-beta-very-long-sha-xyz"}
}
```

maria: Could we normalize service_version into a short id and keep a mapping table? Would cut token count for common versions.

jon: That helps size but hurts ad-hoc debugging — folks often filter by version directly. Join cost vs inline convenience.

ravi: Operational thought: two-tier storage seems promising — hot lane = minimal canonical fields optimized for our common queries/alerts; cold lane = full envelope for deep-dive. Hot lane supports immediate queries/alerts without joins.

taylor: +1, but we must keep cost attribution correct when sampling/late-enriching. Late enrichment mustn't lose billing mapping used for shard routing.

alex: Another angle: compact attribute encoding — short canonical keys and dictionary-encoded values for high-cardinality attrs (like long version strings). We already use similar patterns for embedding metadata.

maria: Caveat: dictionary decoding adds complexity in dashboards and can increase cache misses for ad-hoc queries. Not a showstopper but a cost.

jon: For SLO/alerts we need derived signals (status, latency buckets) in hot lane. Trace-level full text can live in cold lane. That will reduce index pressure.

ravi: Also, for routing at ingest time we need billing_key present. So even if spans don't carry billing_key, envelope.root must. We can avoid span-level duplication.

taylor: Proposal: make billing_key mandatory at root and optional on spans only when it differs from root. That should remove most duplication.

alex: Proposed experiment (schema v2):
- envelope.root: minimal required fields: trace_id, billing_key, service_id, start_ns, duration_ns, tags (short keys)
- spans: id, parent, kind, duration, name_id (dictionary encoded)
- pointer -> full_envelope_bucket/key for cold storage
- migration flag to opt-in

maria: Can you estimate storage savings? My gut says 20-40% for traces by size depending on how chatty attrs are.

jon: I can run a sampler replay job for a day of traces to measure actual size delta and query latency changes for top-10 queries.

ravi: Indexing note: restrict hot-lane indexed fields to a small whitelist and rely on cold-lane join for full-text predicates. Avoid indexing all tags by default.

taylor: Let's add a canonical "query patterns" doc to the obs playbook listing common predicates (service, env, billing_key, trace_id, span_name, error) and ensure hot-lane supports those efficiently.

alex: Operational requirements: maintain sample_reason + sample_weight on root so analytics can do correct extrapolation when we sample at edge.

jon: One more thought: full-text span search is a common user need. We could keep a small span_excerpt (first 256 bytes) in hot lane and keep the full span text in cold lane.

taylor: And Console should indicate whether trace data is hot or cold and provide a "fetch full envelope" button that retrieves from cold lane lazily.

observability-bot: new RFC created: https://github.com/redwood/repo/rfcs/1234 — "compact-trace-schema-v2"

alex: OK — summary of immediate actions: I'll open RFC PR with schema draft + migration plan. jon: run replay job. ravi: write migration runbook. taylor: add Console UX hooks. maria: run perf & size analysis.

maria: I'll review the perf outcomes and verify query latencies on the sampled replay.

jon: I'll post results in this thread when done.

ravi: I'll document rollback steps and a canary migration plan for Dedicated customers.

taylor: I'll mock Console wireframes and include the "fetch full envelope" CTA.

alex: Thanks all. Quick question — sampling interplay: confirm we include sample_reason + sample_weight in hot lane?

maria: Yes, include both.

jon: Added note — include span_excerpt field (<=256 bytes) on hot lane for quick search.

alex: Great. I'll create the PR and tag reviewers. Closing for now :thumbsup:
